main_text.head: DIALOG. V.
De Tentoriis, Fossa, Vallo, Portis.
main_text.p: AVD. Tenet me & oculos hæc species, tota pulchra, prudens, imò sapiens, quod initio dixisti. Unde rusticulis ista mens? nam tales putantur prisci Romani: etsi multa sub regibus, quæ & cor & elegantiam ostendunt. LIPS. Nobis sic videntur, fateor: sed velim examinari à peritis & Martialibus; quia, vt Fabius ait, tum dignum opera pretium venit, cum inter se congruunt præcepta & experimenta. Sed examinari dico ab iis, qui non omnium litterarum aut artium rudes: in quos profecto conuenit ——{*}νῆς ἐχ ἑνὶ κενταύρῳς[?]. At nos, si lubet,Mem nō inest Centaurū. pergamus: enucleanda etiam quædam in his Castris.

His ita constitutis, tota figura castrorum sit quadrata, æquilatera. Partes autem eius & in strigarum sectione, & in alio ordine, vbi similem locationem habent. Vallum vero ipsum abiungunt à tentoriis quaquaversus pedes ducentos. Id vacuum multas & spectabiles utilitates iis præbet, quoniam & ad egressus in-POLYB.

page.notes: Greek column is set in a cursive, close type; several letters and accents are doubtful and are not individually marked, so the Greek transcription is approximate and needs checking against the scan. The note reference at "in quos profecto conuenit" is printed as an asterisk; the Greek after it may end in "κενταύρῳς" but the final letters are uncertain. Left column breaks at "ἐξα-" and continues on the next page. The side label "POLYB." in the right margin is treated as a marginal note. The catchword is printed as "gressusque" and is reproduced as "gressusque".
